subtitle: Journal-club style ICU update: PICO, key results, appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English.

script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for November 16, 2026.
Today we will review 3 recent ICU-relevant publications.
The format is quick listen first, then PICO, key results, critical appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English notes.
Use this as a morning triage tool, then open the source link for full-text appraisal before changing practice.

Among 2387 patients, illness severity and chronic kidney disease prevalence increased with age.

AKI developed in 1396 patients (58.5%), rising from 56.2% (60-69 years) to 63.3% (≥80 years); age, MFI (adjusted risk ratio 1.030 per point), and CCI (1.028 per point) were each associated with AKI occurrence.

articles.title: Distinct associations of age, frailty, and comorbidity with AKI occurrence, mortality, and kidney function recovery in older ICU patients: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.summary: Among 2387 patients, illness severity and chronic kidney disease prevalence increased with age. AKI developed in 1396 patients (58.5%), rising from 56.2% (60-69 years) to 63.3% (≥80 years); age, MFI (adjusted risk ratio 1.030 per point), and CCI (1.028 per point) were each associated with AKI occurrence. AKI (hazard ratio 3.135, 95% CI 2.585-3.801) and age (1.039 per year) were associated with in-hospital death, whereas MFI and CCI were not after adjustment for acute illness. Of 927 survivors with AKI, 50.2% recovered by discharge. Acute kidney injury (AKI) is common in critically ill older adults, but the associations of chronological age and baseline vulnerability to kidney outcomes remain uncertain.

articles.title: Coronary Perfusion Pressure During Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation is Associated with Outcomes from Pediatric In-hospital Cardiac Arrest.
articles.summary: Seventy-one (64%) achieved ROSC. Thirty (27%) had CoPP ≥20mmHg. In adjusted models, average CoPP ≥20mmHg was associated with higher rates of ROSC (aRR 1.48 [95%CI 1.12, 1.95]; p=0.005). Multiple animal studies and one adult study establish that coronary perfusion pressure (CoPP) during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is associated with survival outcomes, such as return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). Yet, CoPP during pediatric in-hospital cardiac arrest (pIHCA) has not been investigated.

articles.title: Characterization of Urgent ICU Consultations in the Evaluation of Processes of Care and the Outcomes of Children in Hospital (EPOCH) Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.summary: This is a secondary analysis of patients with one or more ICU consultations. A care episode was defined as consecutive urgent ICU consultations until an ICU admission or at least 2 weeks without an urgent ICU consultation. There were 4288 urgent ICU consultations in 3625 care episodes for 3000 patients with a median (interquartile range) age of 25 months (5-99 mo). In the parent EPOCH trial, hospitals were randomized to Bedside Pediatric Early Warning System or usual care; no intervention was assigned in this secondary analysis. The outcomes of the 3000 last care episodes were in-consultation death in three (0.1%) and urgent ICU admission in 1477 (49.2%).
